episode_title: In the Loop: San Antonio's Culture, Sports, and Tech with Peter Holt, CEO of HoltCat and Managing Partner of Spurs Sports

real_qa.q: What unique cultural advantages does San Antonio have compared to other cities in the United States?
real_qa.r: San Antonio has a real Tex-Mex, Hispanic American culture that goes back hundreds of years and shapes core values including fun and joy, kindness and caring, service, and hard work. These foundational values have led to flourishing industries in military, manufacturing, hospitality, tourism, and biomedical sectors, and now emerging tech and cybersecurity industries are building on this same cultural foundation.
real_qa.requete: San Antonio cultural advantages compared cities

real_qa.q: Why is San Antonio positioned well for tech and startup growth in the next decade?
real_qa.r: San Antonio has a remarkably young demographic compared to other cities, with more college students per capita than many realize. The city also has first-generation college graduates per capita higher than any other city in the country, new leadership across all major universities (UTSA, Trinity, Alamo Colleges, St. Mary's) committed to the future, economic and political leaders rowing in the same direction, existing infrastructure and space to grow, great weather, and less barriers of entry for individuals to make a real impact compared to mature cities like Chicago or San Francisco.
real_qa.requete: San Antonio startup growth demographics advantages

real_qa.q: What infrastructure improvements between Austin and San Antonio are planned to connect the two cities?
real_qa.r: San Antonio is undergoing a $2 billion expansion at the airport, and both cities now have enhanced flight offerings with Austin recently adding direct daily flights to Amsterdam. Peter Holt sees a multimodal transportation strategy as most likely, potentially including light or high-speed rail, tunnels via The Boring Company, or emerging flying vehicle technology before traditional rail is fully implemented.
real_qa.requete: Austin San Antonio transportation rail infrastructure expansion

real_qa.q: What are the three main investment focus areas for Iron Spring Ventures?
real_qa.r: Iron Spring Ventures focuses on autonomy, new energy investment and resources, and supply chain logistics improvement. Holt emphasizes that infrastructure—the computing power, warehouses, electricity, and water systems powering AI and technology—is critical, and Iron Spring aims to increase focus and investment dollars going to the infrastructure side versus just the end-user side.
real_qa.requete: Iron Spring Ventures investment focus areas autonomy energy

real_qa.q: When will fully autonomous electric heavy equipment become available in the construction industry?
real_qa.r: Peter Holt predicts that within the next 10 years there will be autonomous EV heavy equipment with zero human operation on-site. For example, an excavator could receive a CAD drawing input and dig a utility trench 24/7 unattended, requiring human touch only during delivery and pickup, with daily recharging at powered sites like new warehouses or Port San Antonio.
real_qa.requete: autonomous electric excavator heavy equipment 10 years

guest.bio_context: Peter Holt is a native of South Texas, born in Corpus Christi and raised on a horse farm about an hour north of San Antonio. He is co-founder of Iron Spring Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on infrastructure, autonomy, and energy. Holt has deep ties to San Antonio and is raising his family there, bringing both family business leadership and investment expertise to the region.
